 Judge Orders Trump To Give Interview Under Oath In BBC Libel Case
 23/10/2026 02:51 PM 
 LONDON, Oct 23 (Bernama-PA Media/dpa) -- US President Donald Trump must give an interview under oath before the end of the year as part of his US$10 billion defamation case against the BBC, a US court has ruled, reported PA Media/dpa.
 The order by Judge Enjoliqué Lett followed complaints by the broadcaster's legal team that the president had delayed his pre-trial deposition.
 Defence lawyer Charles Tobin said that with two months left on the timetable to disclose evidence "We still haven't been able to depose the plaintiff."
 He pointed out a date October 16 had been agreed to, but Trump cancelled it due to a "matter of national importance."
 Tobin said the president had actually been campaigning in Georgia, adding: "He was participating in party politics and prioritised that over sitting for the deposition."
 Judge Lett said Trump must sit for a deposition by December 11 or face having his lawsuit thrown out - unless the discovery period was extended past December 18.
 Trump is seeking substantial damages in a Florida court over the editing of a "Panorama" documentary from 2024 about the US Capitol riots.
 The documentary has faced criticism for giving the impression the US president had encouraged his supporters to storm the Capitol building on January 6, 2021 after he lost the election to Joe Biden.
 The allegations led the then-BBC director-general Tim Davie to announce his resignation.
 BBC Chairman Samir Shah apologised on behalf of the broadcaster over an "error of judgment" and accepted the editing of the programme gave "the impression of a direct call for violent action."
 However, the broadcaster is seeking to have the case thrown out, warning of the "chilling effect" it would have on "robust reporting on public figures and events."
 It has also challenged the Florida court's jurisdiction to hear the case given the programme was never aired in the state or in the US.
 --BERNAMA-PA MEDIA/dpa
